History:
- 39-year-old male awakened at ~05:30 today by sudden, severe left-sided headache—worse than any previous headache; still present at time of call.
- Prior headaches: intermittent, milder, bilateral/frontal “cluster” type; never strictly unilateral.
- Triggers/associations: 2-month period of significant work stress, late nights; mild photophobia; brief dizziness on rising that resolved; no neck stiffness, fever, nausea, vomiting, or focal neurologic symptoms.
- Headache modestly eases after lying down; no relief from single dose of paracetamol taken this morning.
- No family history of migraine; no recent head trauma.

Past Medical History:
- Generalised anxiety disorder (≈2 years).
- No hypertension, cardiovascular, or other chronic illnesses noted.
- Allergies: none known.
- Medications:
  • Sertraline – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Paracetamol (single dose today) – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Telephone consultation; no direct examination performed.
- Patient-reported negatives: no neck stiffness, no fever, no nausea/vomiting, no photophobia severe enough to incapacitate, no focal weakness or sensory changes.
- Mental status: alert, oriented; mood generally stable; denies suicidal ideation.

Impression:
- Probable primary headache disorder—most consistent with migraine without aura vs tension-type headache.
  • Migraine: unilateral pain, photophobia, stress/sleep deprivation trigger.
  • Tension headache: ongoing occupational stress, prior similar but milder headaches.
- Serious secondary causes (e.g., subarachnoid haemorrhage) appear unlikely on history but counselled patient on red-flag symptoms.

Management Plan:
- Pharmacologic:
  • Initiate ibuprofen (higher migraine-effective dosing) – dose/route/frequency not documented; may continue paracetamol if desired.
- Lifestyle / supportive:
  • Self-certify and consider 1 week off work to reduce stress.
  • Ensure ≥7–8 hours sleep nightly.
  • Maintain hydration: 1.5–2 L non-caffeinated fluids daily.
  • Link provided for local counselling service for stress/anxiety support.
- Education:
  • Written summary plus list of headache “danger signs” supplied; instructed to seek immediate care if such symptoms develop.
- Follow-up:
  • Telephone review in 1 week; sooner if headache worsens, new symptoms arise, or inadequate relief.

Patient Summary:
Mr Warren experienced a new, severe left-sided headache this morning that woke him from sleep. History is most suggestive of a migraine precipitated by prolonged work-related stress and poor sleep. Ibuprofen therapy, rest, hydration, and stress reduction measures have been advised, with follow-up in one week.

Key Takeaways:
- Start ibuprofen today for pain; continue paracetamol only if needed.
- Prioritise rest, adequate sleep, and 1.5–2 L water daily.
- Seek urgent care if headache becomes sudden/thunderclap in nature, is accompanied by fever, neck stiffness, visual changes, weakness, or vomiting.

Next Steps:
- Reassess in 1 week; consider blood tests or further imaging if headaches persist or worsen.
- Engage with counselling services; evaluate need for further anxiety management.
